name: application-comfortable-list-row
title: Comfortable List Row
description: Spacious two-line list row with a leading avatar, title/subtitle pair, and trailing meta text with a chevron — the "comfortable" density variant of a list item.
useWhen: Listing people, contacts, or generic navigable items where generous spacing and a two-line title/subtitle improve scannability.
The row navigates somewhere on click/tap (it's an anchor with a chevron), not a media-playback row.
You want a density that reads as roomy and touch-friendly rather than compact/data-dense.
avoidWhen: You're listing playable media (tracks, episodes) with a play button — use `media-object-row` for that unrelated, action-specific pattern.
You need a high-density list to fit many items on screen — this row's generous padding works against that; use a tighter row pattern instead.
The row doesn't navigate anywhere — drop the chevron and the anchor semantics rather than implying navigation that doesn't happen.
responsiveBehavior: Single-column list at a fixed max width; the subtitle truncates with an ellipsis before the trailing meta/chevron ever wraps or gets squeezed.
accessibility: Each row is a real <a> wrapping the full row content, giving the entire row a single large hit target and correct link semantics rather than a click handler on a div.
The chevron is aria-hidden since it's a directional affordance, not additional information beyond "this row navigates further."
Title and subtitle are separate text nodes (not a single concatenated string) so screen readers pause naturally between the person's name and their role.

variants.title: Comfortable List Row
variants.description: Three people rows with avatar, name/role, relative time, and a chevron.
accessibility: The full row is one hit target via a wrapping <a>, avoiding small, hard-to-hit click zones on trailing meta or chevron alone.

variants.title: Comfortable List Row (Dark)
variants.description: Comfortable list row adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Meta text and chevron colors are tuned to stay legible but recessive against the dark surface, keeping the title as the primary read.
